How to Migrate to Shopify Plus?

Please don’t think that Migrating to Shopify Plus would be quite an easy copy-paste job. Because you’ll be moving to a completely different platform, with your data, entire design, SEO, and even the integrations.

When done right, the store gets on the path of growth, and on the contrary, when done wrong, it will cost you your rankings, customers & revenue.

For that reason, there should be a clear plan and the right Shopify Plus migration partner who can help you migrate the store quite seamlessly.

Here’s what the migration process looks like at a comparatively high level:

  • Auditing and backing up your current store data
  • Setting up your new Shopify Plus environment
  • Migrating products, customers, orders, and content
  • Handling SEO redirects and preserving your search rankings
  • Testing thoroughly and launching with confidence

We’ll get into the detailed step-by-step migration plan a little further in this guide. But first, let’s make sure the timing is right for you, about migrating, like when you should migrate to Shopify Plus.

When Should You Migrate to Shopify Plus?

The truth is not every business needs Shopify Plus, but when you start facing these roadblocks, it’s time to consider the migration.

  1. At peak hours, the store gets crashed.
  2. You’ve outgrown your platform’s features, and now you are in dire need of custom checkout flows, advanced automation, or seamless ERP and CRM integrations.
  3. Maintenance costs are piling up, and you have to patch up.
  4. When you’re expanding globally, in that case, only Shopify Plus can help you get support in 175 countries, 21 languages & multi-currency pricing out of the box.
  5. Your checkout is costing you sales. With Shop Pay and Shopify’s customizable checkout, you can boost conversions by up to 18%. If your current checkout is clunky or limited, you’re leaving money on the table.

How to Prepare for the Migration to Shopify Plus?

Before stepping up for the migration, you should have a Shopify Plus migration checklist like this;

  1. Audit your current store. Take a full inventory of everything that needs to move — products, customer data, order history, blog content, landing pages, active discount codes, and third-party app integrations. This is also a great time to clean house and leave behind anything outdated or redundant.
  2. Back everything up. Before you touch anything, export and back up all your data. This is non-negotiable.
  3. Set clear migration goals. Are you migrating purely for performance? Better checkout? Global expansion? Knowing your goals helps you prioritize what matters most during the migration.
  4. Create a data field mapping document. Every platform structures data differently. Map out how your current fields translate to Shopify — for example, how product categories become Shopify collections, or how customer fields align.
  5. Set a realistic timeline. A simple migration can take 4–6 weeks. A complex one with custom features, large catalogs, or multiple integrations can take 3–6 months. Plan your migration around low-traffic periods to minimize business disruption.

With solid preparation in place, you’re ready to move into the actual migration process. And once you have gone through the checklist, please follow this 5-step migration plan.

5 Step Migration Plan

Here’s a straightforward Shopify Plus Migration guide you can follow, whether you’re coming from Magento, WooCommerce, Salesforce, or any other platform.

Step 1: Migrate Your Data

Start with your product catalog; it’s the foundation of your store. Keep your existing SKUs and product URLs consistent to avoid SEO headaches. Then migrate customers (note: passwords can’t be migrated due to encryption differences, so plan to send reactivation emails). Historical orders follow, though Shopify doesn’t support direct order imports, use a third-party migration tool, or keep historical records in a CRM.

Your migration method depends on your store size: CSV exports work well for smaller stores, migration apps like Cart2Cart or LitExtension are great for mid-size operations, and for large or complex stores, API-based migration with expert support is the most reliable route.

Step 2: Set Up Your Shopify Plus Store

Sign up for Shopify Plus and configure your store settings from the ground up. Set your primary currency early; Shopify locks it once transactions begin. Define your tax rules, shipping rates, and payment gateways. Set up staff accounts with the right permission levels for developers, marketers, and support teams.

If you’re selling internationally, this is the stage to set up Shopify Plus expansion stores with localised pricing, languages, and tax settings for each market.

Step 3: Design and Development

Choose whether to rebuild your existing storefront or start fresh with a new design. Shopify Plus offers 100+ themes and deep customisation through its Liquid template language. Install only the apps you genuinely need; too many apps slow your store down. Custom integrations with ERPs, CRMs, or third-party tools can be built via Shopify’s extensive API.

Step 4: Shopify Plus Migration SEO

This step is critical and one of the most commonly mishandled. Set up 301 redirects from all your old URLs to the new ones. Keep page titles, meta descriptions, and image alt text intact. Verify your structured data (schema markup) is properly implemented. Once you go live, submit your new XML sitemap via Google Search Console and monitor for crawl errors.

Migrations with a fully mapped redirect plan recover 92–98% of organic traffic within 60–90 days. Without one, it can take six months or more. Don’t skip this step.

Step 5: Test, Launch, and Optimise

Before going live, set up a staging environment and test everything: product search, cart functionality, checkout flows, payment gateways, email notifications, mobile responsiveness, and all custom features. Run stress tests to simulate peak traffic conditions.

For launch, a soft rollout is generally safer for complex stores; it gives you real-world testing time before full exposure. Communicate the transition to your customers via email and social, choose a low-traffic window, and monitor performance closely in the days after launch.

Benefits of Migrating to Shopify Plus

Still weighing up whether the move is worth it? Here’s what you get on the other side of a Shopify Plus migration:

  • Enterprise-grade performance. 99.99% uptime, unlimited bandwidth, and a global CDN, your store stays fast and online no matter what.
  • Powerful automation. Shopify Flow lets you automate inventory management, order processing, customer segmentation, and more, saving your team thousands of hours.
  • Customisable checkout. Shopify Plus gives you full control over your checkout experience. Pair it with Shop Pay, and you’ve got the fastest, most converting checkout on the market.
  • Lower transaction fees. At just 0.15%, Shopify Plus transaction fees are significantly lower than platforms like Salesforce (which charges 1–3% of GMV). For high-volume stores, the savings are substantial.
  • Global selling made easy. Sell in 175 countries, 21 languages, with multi-currency support and localised storefronts, all from a single account.
  • Up to 80% less infrastructure cost. No more server maintenance, manual patches, or costly upgrades. Shopify Plus handles it all so you can reinvest in growth.
  • Free sandbox environment. Test new features, themes, and integrations without risking your live store.
  • 24/7 priority support. Access dedicated account managers and round-the-clock expert support whenever you need it.

Why You Should Work With a Shopify Plus Partner for Migration?

Technically, you can attempt a Shopify Plus migration on your own. But if your store has a large product catalog, custom integrations, complex data, or significant SEO equity, going solo carries real risk.

A certified Shopify Plus Partner brings the technical expertise, tested processes, and hands-on experience to handle every aspect of the migration, from data mapping and SEO preservation to custom development and post-launch support. They’ve seen the common pitfalls before and know exactly how to avoid them.

Whether you’re moving from Magento, WooCommerce, Salesforce, or a custom-built platform, the team at Dynamic Dreamz knows exactly what it takes to make your Shopify Plus migration a success.

When you work with Dynamic Dreamz as your Shopify Plus migration partner, you get a team that handles everything, so you can focus on what you do best: growing your business.

Conclusion

Whenever you’re migrating to Shopify Plus, you make one of the most impactful decisions ever for your growing ecommerce business. So, yes, it’s not and never can be a simple platform upgrade, but a step forward for better operations, seamless customer experiences, and toward lightening-fast growth.

And yes, not everyone has to go through the migration process, and if you do, then please ensure to follow the checklist and the steps listed above. Or else you can just connect with us, your best Shopify Plus migration partner, and let them do their job.

FAQ

How much does a Shopify Plus migration cost?

Shopify Plus plans basically start at $2,000/month, and that’s not the migration costs, because it can vary based on the current platform you have, store complexity, custom feature requirements, and whether or not you want to work with a migration agency.

How long does it take to migrate to Shopify Plus?

A straightforward migration would typically take roughly 4 to 6 weeks. Larger or more complex migrations, involving custom features, multiple integrations, and large datasets, can take anywhere from 3–6 months.

Can I migrate from WooCommerce to Shopify Plus?

People ask about Can and How to migrate from WooCommerce to Shopify Plus, so, yes, you can, and people do that more often.

Can I migrate from Magento to Shopify Plus?

Yes, and many businesses do, with their queries of “How to migrate from Magento to Shopify Plus.” And once their queries are resolved by their Shopify Plus Partner, they will move forward on the path of migration.

Will I lose my SEO rankings when I migrate to Shopify Plus?

Not if your migration is handled correctly. The key is setting up 301 redirects for all changed URLs, preserving your metadata, keeping alt text intact, and verifying your structured data post-launch. Migrations with a proper redirect plan in place recover the vast majority of organic traffic within 60–90 days.

Do I need a Shopify Plus Partner to migrate?

For small stores with minimal integrations, a DIY migration may be feasible. But for businesses with large catalogs, custom functionality, or significant SEO equity, working with a certified Shopify Plus migration partner is the smarter and safer choice. The cost of getting it wrong, lost data, SEO drops, broken integrations, almost always outweighs the cost of expert help.
